solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old vehicle number occupying Russian car for all to see

indicators.note: to occupy a space is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for number
the Lada is a Russian car make
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A vintage vehicle registration plate displayed on a Russian car, visible to every passer-by.
explanation.walkthrough: N sits inside LADA to give LANDA, then U (the universal film rating in Britain) finishes LANDAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood, a historic form of transport.

clue.text: The Gunners start to struggle and 50 leave stadium

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
whatever leaves goes away, so those letters are taken out of the bigger word

blocks.note: Arsenal Football Club is nicknamed the Gunners
opening letter of struggle
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Arsenal, the London football club, begin to falter and fifty fans walk out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S and L from ARSENAL and ARENA remains. Arsenal is a London football club whose nickname is the Gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue with tiered seating for sport or spectacle, much like a stadium.

clue.text: The deal for cruising on liner is everlasting

indicators.note: cruising means wandering about aimlessly, so these letters drift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
SS stands for steamship, and a liner is one

explanation.surface: An ad claims the holiday offer on an ocean liner is too good to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the steamship after the reshuffled letters; 'cruising' looks like part of the holiday but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never dies is immortal, lasting for ever, which is what everlasting describes.

clue.text: Type of clothing seen in college congress

blocks.note: uni is short for university
congress in its older sense of sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: A fashion style spotted at a student conference or assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like a political gathering, but here it means intercourse, as in the phrase sexual congress.
explanation.definitionFit: Unisex garments are designed to be worn by both men and women, describing a kind of apparel.

clue.text: Stolen case? Outside, five principal characters suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so the letters are in a wrong order
being outside means surrounding, so one group of letters wraps round another

blocks.note: the first five letters of the alphabet
a case for luggage is a bag

explanation.surface: A detective muses on a theft: outside it, five leading players are suspects.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'principal characters' are letters of the alphabet, not people in a drama; rearranged as CAB...ED they hold BAG. To cabbage is British slang for pilfering.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbage as a verb is old tailors' slang for pinching leftover cloth, so something cabbaged has been pilfered.

clue.text: Challenged short search on island done carelessly

indicators.note: work carried out carelessly is jumbled and untidy, so the letters come out in disorder

blocks.note: short-tempered means cross
a quest is a search
I is the abbreviation for island
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hurried search of an island is carried out sloppily and then questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short search' reads as one idea, a brief search, but 'short' is its own piece meaning bad-tempered. In a down clue 'on' puts the search above the island.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cross-questioned is to be interrogated closely, typically in court, with one's account disputed and tested.

clue.text: Toiled to create a section of body by sculpture

blocks.note: a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders
taken as written
the gut is part of the body's digestive tract

explanation.surface: A sculptor works hard to carve part of a torso for a statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means beside: the bust sits alongside the other two pieces, coming first in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bust a gut is an informal idiom for making a huge effort, and toiled means worked very hard.

clue.text: Nag heard disturbing regulars in taproom, causing bother

indicators.note: regulars suggests letters at regular intervals, every other one taken
something heard is spoken, so we want letters that sound like the word
to disturb is to break in on, so one piece intrudes into the middle of another

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of taproom
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, and a nag is a horse; the letters GG say it

explanation.surface: Someone overheard nagging the pub regulars, stirring up trouble in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a verb about scolding, but it is a horse, a gee-gee, and GG spoken aloud is that word. The regulars are alternate letters, not drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggravation, trouble or hassle, and bother means much the same kind of fuss.

clue.text: Scotch addict upset officer — getting the consequences?

definitions.note: plural against a singular answer; the question mark admits the looseness

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, so in a down clue the word is turned upside down

blocks.note: to scotch a plan is to put an end to it
an addict is a drug user
Lt is short for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A whisky-loving addict annoys a police officer, and then faces what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky beside 'addict', but it is the verb meaning to put a stop to something.
explanation.definitionFit: The end result is the final outcome of a process, what follows from actions, as consequences do.

clue.text: Doing a turn say, Hispanic type bends like rubber?

indicators.note: a turn swings something round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, which is what say means
a Latino is a person of Latin American origin
U-bends and S-bends are both kinds of bend in a pipe

explanation.surface: A dancer performing a routine, perhaps Hispanic, bends as if made of rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bends' are two separate letters, from the U-bend and the S-bend. The question mark flags that rubber is only an approximate example of jelly-like texture.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatinous means jelly-like, wobbly and elastic in consistency, a texture loosely comparable to rubber, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Leave surgeon in theatre area

blocks.note: to leave is to go
DS is the abbreviation for dental surgeon

explanation.surface: An instruction for a surgeon to leave the operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests an operating theatre beside 'surgeon', but it is a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The gods is the highest gallery in a playhouse, where the cheapest seats are, far up near the ceiling.

clue.text: News updates about remains, at half-nine, showing indiscretion

indicators.note: half of a word keeps just one of its two halves, here the back pair
about means around, so one piece is placed round the others

blocks.note: RSS is the web feed format that delivers news updates
ash is what remains after burning, as with cremated remains
the second half of nine

explanation.surface: Breaking news about human remains, released at half past nine, was indiscreet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At half-nine' reads as a time of day, but it asks for half the word nine. RSS, a web news feed, wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashness is acting hastily without thought for consequences, which is a lack of prudence or indiscretion.

clue.text: Type of map acquired with foreign currency’s used for archipelago

blocks.note: an A to Z is a street map book
öre is a Scandinavian coin; with the 's it becomes ORE'S

explanation.surface: A traveller buys a map using foreign money to explore a group of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s is read as 'is', attached to the currency. An A to Z is a British street-atlas brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Azores are a Portuguese island group in the mid-Atlantic, a chain of islands forming an archipelago.

clue.text: Learner in Lincoln practised

indicators.note: being in something means sitting within it, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: Abe is the familiar name of President Abraham Lincoln
L is the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: A student in the city of Lincoln rehearsed their skills.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city, but it is the US president, Abe.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone practised at a task is skilled and competent, having the capacity to do it well.

clue.text: Kindle, due to being mishandled, ineffective

indicators.note: something mishandled is treated roughly and messed up, so the letters get jumbled

blocks.note: to kindle a fire is to make it burn
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An e-reader stopped working because it was treated roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindle looks like the Amazon e-reader brand, but it is the verb meaning to set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something burned out is exhausted and spent, no longer able to function or produce results.

clue.text: Unionist contrived to eradicate parking that’s exorbitant

indicators.note: to eradicate is to wipe out entirely, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for Unionist
spurious means false or fabricated
P is the road-sign symbol for parking

explanation.surface: A politician schemes to scrap parking charges that are far too high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrived' looks like a verb in the story of scheming, but it is the adjective meaning fake. U is the abbreviation for a Unionist in Northern Irish politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurious describes lending at extortionate interest rates, and more broadly any grossly excessive charge or price.

clue.text: Spontaneous monkey frolicking with workers

blocks.note: a monkey is a mischievous child, an imp
a romp is a spell of frolicking
TU is a trade union, a body of workers

explanation.surface: A monkey playfully cavorting alongside labourers, all on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frolicking' looks like a signal to rearrange the monkey, but it simply means a romp.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done without preparation or planning, on the spur of the moment, which is spontaneous.

clue.text: Bread basket starts to fill up — loaf makes excess

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, one kept from each

blocks.note: bread basket is slang for the stomach
the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A baker's bread basket starts to fill up as loaves pile up in abundance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' is part of the baking picture but only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a bellyful of something means having more than enough of it, a surfeit or too much.

clue.text: European city that’s less urban, somewhat regressive

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the phrase is used
to regress is to go backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the letters running from the end of that's to the start of urban

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a European capital that is more rustic and somewhat backward.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the letters from right to left across the three words to find the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Brussels is the capital of Belgium and seat of the main European Union institutions.

clue.text: Track comprises mass of dung heaps primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: a cowpat is a mass of dung
opening letter of heaps

explanation.surface: A farm trail made up of piles of manure.
explanation.walkthrough: A pat on its own is a flat lump of dung, as in cowpat.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a narrow way or trail for walking along, which is one sense of track.

clue.text: Swift retracing river snapped by watcher?

indicators.note: to retrace steps is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards
something snapped up by another is caught and held, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a spy watches covertly
the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

explanation.surface: A swift, the bird, flying back up a river and photographed by a birdwatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like the bird in a river scene with a watcher, but it is the adjective. The Dee is a common crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy and swift are synonyms, both describing something that moves or happens quickly.

clue.text: London area curtailed crush — film later showing?

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the final letter is lopped off

blocks.note: SE is the south-east London postcode area
to quell a revolt is to crush it

explanation.surface: A packed crowd in a London district queues for a late screening of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' seems to go with the London area, but it trims the following word. 'Crush' looks like a crowd, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequel is a follow-up movie continuing an earlier story, released and screened afterwards, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Scientific apparatus website declaimed

indicators.note: to declaim is to speak out loud, so the sound matters rather than spelling

blocks.note: YouTube is the video-sharing website

explanation.surface: A lab device being promoted loudly on a video-sharing website.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter U is pronounced like 'you', so the website's name and the lab item sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-tube is a bent glass tube shaped like the letter, used in laboratories as a manometer or for experiments.

clue.text: One asks scamp to hide mineral in both hands

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it within, so one piece is concealed inside another

blocks.note: a scamp is a mischievous child, an imp
L and R stand for left and right
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: Someone asks a young rascal to hide a stone between his two hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both hands' means left and right, as the letters L and R, split round the mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: An implorer is a person who begs or pleads urgently, so is someone who asks earnestly.

clue.text: Follow varying directions on outskirts in Ukraine

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges of a place, so the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: east, north and south, three different compass points
the first and last letters of Ukraine

explanation.surface: Tracking different routes around the edges of a Ukrainian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Varying' only signals that the compass points are different ones; each direction is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to happen afterwards as a result, coming after in sequence, which is one sense of follow.

clue.text: Common name, reflecting one from Madrid

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the letters appear backwards

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
uno is Spanish for one

explanation.surface: A widespread Spanish name, reflecting someone from Madrid.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang, from 1950s class commentary, for speech or habits not typical of the upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U usage marks someone as not upper class, so common in the snobbish sense of vulgar or lowly.

clue.text: Pointer having to play with mail

blocks.note: to finger something is to toy with it
post is the British word for mail

explanation.surface: A pet dog, a pointer, playing with the letters that arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' looks like the gun dog breed, but it is a signpost.
explanation.definitionFit: A fingerpost is a signpost whose arms are shaped like pointing hands, directing travellers the way to go.

clue.text: Church can be so extreme — watch display

blocks.note: a steep price is an extreme one
a digital watch face uses an LED, a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: A church ceremony can be so over the top, a real show to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase: a church may be described as this, having a tower with a spire.
explanation.definitionFit: A steepled building has a tall spired tower, a feature many churches possess, so the adjective fits churches.

clue.text: Returned the empty onto float? Sure

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its insides, so only its outer letters remain
something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: first and last letters of the
a buoy is a float moored in water

explanation.surface: Asked whether you took the empties back on the milk float, you answer: certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk float is a British electric delivery van, and the empties are returned bottles, but here the float is a buoy.
explanation.definitionFit: You bet is an informal exclamation of emphatic agreement, meaning certainly or of course, as sure does.
